title: Rosewater and glycerin face mist
subtitle: A light hydrating spray for clean skin
excerpt: Rosewater face mist is a simple toning spray made from distilled rosewater, vegetable glycerin, and still water at a 10% glycerin concentration. Spritzed onto clean skin, it draws a light layer of moisture to the skin surface without leaving an oily film. Makes 100 ml in a small glass spray bottle; keeps three months at room temperature or six months in the fridge.
sourceNotes: Glycerin as a humectant in skincare: Cosmetics & Toiletries industry review (2015); glycerin at 10% is the standard toning-mist concentration, above 20% can feel tacky. Rose water as a toning base: Organic Beauty by Margo Marrone (2013). Preservative note: this formula contains water and is at risk of microbial contamination without a preservative; adding 1% broad-spectrum preservative (e.g. Optiphen Plus) extends shelf life to 6 months at room temperature and is recommended for larger batches or shared use.

recipe.yieldDescription: 100 ml in a small spray bottle
recipe.batchNotes: Add 1% broad-spectrum preservative (Optiphen or Geogard) if making larger batches or using for more than one person.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: For personal use, small batches kept in the fridge are safest without a preservative. Make a fresh 100 ml batch monthly.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Three months at room temperature; six months refrigerated. This formula contains water and no preservative, discard if the liquid turns cloudy, develops a film, or smells off. Add a broad-spectrum preservative for longer shelf life.

glossaryTerms.definition: An ingredient that draws moisture from the surrounding air or the deeper layers of the skin to the surface, keeping the outer layer hydrated. Vegetable glycerin is one of the most common cosmetic humectants.

content.text: Combine the rosewater, distilled water, and vegetable glycerin in a small bowl or jug. Stir until the glycerin has fully dissolved, glycerin is thick and needs a minute of stirring. Add the preservative if using and stir again. Pour into the spray bottle using a small funnel. Label with the date.

Spray onto clean skin from 20 to 30 cm away, two or three spritzes is enough. Leave to dry before applying moisturiser. Can also be used as a midday refresh over makeup, the fine mist does not disturb most pressed powders.
Three months at room temperature; six months refrigerated (without preservative). Discard if the liquid turns cloudy or smells off.
